سَقَّاطٌ (S, Sgh, L, K) and ↓ سَقَاطٌ , (K,) or سَقَّاطٌ وَرَآءَ الضَّرِيبَةِ, (M,) A sword that falls behind the object struck therewith, cutting it so as to pass to the ground: (S, K:) or that cuts the object struck therewith, and then reaches to what is after it: (M, K:) or that cleaves so as to reach to the ground after cutting: (IAar, M:) or that passes through the object struck therewith, and then falls. (Expos. of the Deewán of the Hudhalees.) ＝
-A2- See سَقَطِىٌّ, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
